(Adnkronos) – Another day of bad weather in Italy. For tomorrow, Tuesday, November 17, there are a total of 7 regions for which the Civil Protection has issued a weather alert: orange for Tuscany and yellow for sectors of Valle d’Aosta, Liguria, Tuscany, Emilia-Romagna, Umbria and Campania. Precisely in Tuscany, where the risk of thunderstorms is stronger, many municipalities have decided to keep schools closed for safety reasons. Here is the updated list.
Schools closed tomorrow in Aulla, Bagnone, Fivizzano, Licciana Nardi, Villafranca in Lunigiana, Pontremoli, Bagni di Lucca. Here, the mayors have already signed specific ordinances providing for the suspension of lessons due to bad weather, but the list could increase during the evening.
Intense Atlantic currents affect a large part of the central-western Mediterranean, causing, tomorrow, a new deterioration with rain starting from the westernmost sectors and an intensification of ventilation from the western quadrants over a large part of the country. Based on available forecasts, the Civil Protection Department, in agreement with the regions involved – which are responsible for activating civil protection systems in the affected territories – has issued a severe weather warning.
The warning forecasts from the early hours of tomorrow, Tuesday, November 17, scattered to widespread precipitation, also in the form of showers or thunderstorms, initially over Valle d’Aosta, extending in the morning to Liguria, Emilia-Romagna and Tuscany. The phenomena will be accompanied by intense downpours, strong wind gusts and frequent electrical activity. From tomorrow morning, strong to gale-force winds with a predominant south-westerly component are also expected over eastern Liguria, Emilia-Romagna, Umbria, Marche and Lazio. Possible storm surges along the west-exposed coasts. Based on the phenomena in progress and forecast, an orange alert for hydrogeological risk has been evaluated for tomorrow on sectors of Tuscany; a yellow weather-hydro alert on sectors of Valle d’Aosta, Liguria, Tuscany, Emilia-Romagna, Umbria and Campania.
